My land is 8 mu, all flat, the same land my family has farmed for generations. Every family in my village grows winter wheat and summer corn — that is what the grain buyers come for, that is what I know how to do. My neighbor's son studied agriculture but he still grows the same things we do. I do not need to think hard about what to grow. The question is just how much to put in and when.

For wheat, I plant in October, just like always. I will use the Jimai 22 seed I bought from the county seed shop — it is the variety everyone here uses now, the village head said the government recommends it. Before planting I will turn the ground with the rented tractor, then put down base fertilizer. My son told me last year I put too much fertilizer and it was a waste of money, so this time I will put a little less on the topdressing in spring. I water four times: before planting to wet the soil, once in winter to protect the roots from freezing, once when the stem is growing in spring, and once when the heads come out. I spray for aphids and rust usually twice — once in April, once closer to harvest if I see problems.

After wheat harvest in June, I plant corn immediately on the same ground. I use hybrid seed from the shop. Corn does not need as much water because summer has more rain, but I will water once or twice if August is dry like last year. I do not plough for corn — I seed directly into the wheat stubble with the planter my village cooperative has. I spray once for borers.

I expect a normal year. Nothing fancy. Just steady.
